title: Japan's 'Donald McDonald' Officially Becomes 'Ronald'
paragraphs: Ronald McDonald has been the face of McDonald's for decades. But if you grew up in Japan, you may know him by a different name — Donald.
On October 1, McDonald's Japan announced that the famous clown would now be called Ronald McDonald in Japan too — just like everywhere else.

Ronald McDonald first appeared in 1963, and is one of America's best-known characters. In his 2001 book Fast Food Nation, Eric Schlosser said one survey even found that 96% of American children knew who Ronald McDonald was — making him second only to Santa Claus!
But when Japan's first McDonald's opened in 1971, its popular mascot got a new name: "Donald McDonald."
Well, it's believed "Donald" was easier for Japanese people to say.
In Japanese, "Ronald" becomes "Ronarudo." And as Kotaku's Brian Ashcraft writes, a "ro" sound quickly followed by a "ru" sound doesn't roll off the tongue quite as easily as "Donarudo" does.
And with McDonald's becoming "Makudonarudo" in Japan, "Donarudo Makudonarudo" just looked and sounded nicer when written and spoken in Japanese.

After more than 50 years as Donald, the change to Ronald surprised many Japanese people. Online, some said it would take time to get used to the new name, while others said they would probably keep calling him Donald anyway.
And one person on X had a different theory: "I think he didn't want to have the same first name as Trump."
Still, after so many years, Donald may be hard for Japanese fans to forget — no matter what McDonald's calls him.
